successor: Hallstatt B2-3 (Late Bronze Age Urnfield phase)
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Urnfield culture' - https://www.britannica.com/topic/Urnfield-culture
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Hallstatt culture' - https://www.britannica.com/topic/Hallstatt-culture

successor: Seleucid Empire (Seleucus I), then Ptolemy Keraunos at Lysimacheia
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Lysimachus' - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Lysimachus
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 11th ed., 'Lysimachus', 1911 (Wikisource) - https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Lysimachus
notes: Execution of Agathocles (c. 284-282) triggered city revolts and defections; Seleucus invaded and killed Lysimachus at Corupedium, 281 BCE. Seleucus was murdered near Lysimacheia months later by Ptolemy Keraunos, who took Thrace and Macedon.

successor: Republic of India (Garo Hills district, Assam)
source1: West Garo Hills District Administration, 'History' - https://westgarohills.gov.in/history/
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Garo' - https://www.britannica.com/topic/Garo
notes: Tura-based district administration created under British rule continued under India after 1947; the Garo Hills district persisted until split in 1976. No break found at 1956; end date looks arbitrary. Evidence thin.

source1: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'ELAM i. The history of Elam' - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/elam-i
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Shutruk-Nahhunte' - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Shutruk-Nahhunte
notes: Igihalkid line (to c. 1210 BCE) followed by the Shutrukid dynasty as kings of Anshan and Susa: dynastic change within the Elamite state, no known foreign conquest. Database successor 'Neo-Assyrian Empire' is wrong.

successor: Egypt - Mamluk Sultanate II (same Turkish/Qalawunid sultanate)
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Egypt: The Mamluk and Ottoman periods (1250-1800)' - https://www.britannica.com/place/Egypt/The-Mamluk-and-Ottoman-periods-1250-1800

successor: Aztec Empire (Triple Alliance of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco, Tlacopan)
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Mexico: The rise of the Aztecs' - https://www.britannica.com/place/Mexico/The-rise-of-the-Aztecs

notes: Tepanec hegemony of Azcapotzalco overthrown 1428 by its own tributaries (Mexica paid it tribute) allied with Texcoco and Tlacopan; Huexotzinco aid never controlled the core. Q4: Tepanec-Texcoco war 1418, Maxtla's 1426 usurpation. DB end 1426.

successor: Kingdom of Saba (continued at Marib until Himyarite annexation c. 275 CE)
source1: Jeremie Schiettecatte, 'Saba'', Thematic Dictionary of Ancient Arabia (2024) - https://ancientarabia.huma-num.fr/dictionary/definition/saba
source2: Alessandra Avanzini, 'Qataban', Thematic Dictionary of Ancient Arabia - https://ancientarabia.huma-num.fr/dictionary/definition/qataban
notes: From the 5th c. BCE Saba lost hegemony (mukarrib title replaced by king) as Qataban and Hadramawt rose, but the kingdom persisted at Marib until Himyar absorbed it c. 270-275 CE. Qataban never held Marib. Chronology debated.

successor: Timurid Empire (Timur, Barlas amir of the Chaghatay ulus)

successor: Egypt - Late Old Kingdom (6th Dynasty, Teti)
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Unas' - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Unas

successor: Kingdom of Aksum (Aksumite-installed king, then Abraha)

notes: Aksumite army crushed Himyar c. 525 (Gajda: c. 522), killed king Yusuf and installed a client king; Aksumite general Abraha then ruled; Sasanians took Yemen c. 570. Q4: Yusuf seized power c. 522 by fighting the Aksumite-backed order.

notes: Emergent Mississippian (Terminal Late Woodland) village phase in the American Bottom, no recorded central authority. Occupation continuous; pre-Mississippian villages persisted until Lohmann-phase reorganization c. 1050, so 900 is a phase division. Indirect evidence only.

successor: Saba under highland-tribe kings at Marib (rival Himyarite kingdom kept Zafar)

successor: Kingdom of Prussia (Warsaw, after Russian occupation 1794-96), with Russia and Austria
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Partitions of Poland' - https://www.britannica.com/event/Partitions-of-Poland

successor: Maukharis and Later Guptas (former Gupta feudatories) in Magadha
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Gupta dynasty' and 'Maukhari dynasty' - https://www.britannica.com/topic/Gupta-dynasty ; https://www.britannica.com/topic/Maukhari-dynasty
source2: A. D. H. Bivar, 'Hephthalites', Encyclopaedia Iranica (2003) - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/hephthalites ; also Britannica 'Mihirakula' - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Mihirakula
notes: Huna (Alkhan) invasions hit the west but were repelled by Guptas and Yasodharman; Magadha not conquered. Empire dwindled as feudatories (Maukharis, Later Guptas) became independent; Maukharis gained some control of Magadha. Last main-line king c.540-550.

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Parantaka I' - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Parantaka-I
notes: Chola Parantaka I (r. 907-c.955), 'destroyer of Madurai', defeated Pandya Rajasimha and Sri Lankan allies (Vellur, c.915), annexing the Pandya country; the king fled to Lanka. Second source could not be opened (fetch rate-limited).

successor: Kahuripan Kingdom (Airlangga, from 1019) after sack by Haji Wurawari of Lwaram
notes: Pucangan inscription: vassal Haji Wurawari of Lwaram sacked capital Wwatan c.1016 (older reading 1006), killing Dharmawangsa; Airlangga refounded the kingdom 1019. Srivijayan instigation hypothesised (would make T2). No scholarly page could be opened (rate limits).

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'ancient Egypt: The Second Intermediate Period' (13th dynasty c.1759-c.1630 BCE; 15th dynasty c.1630-c.1530 BCE) - https://www.britannica.com/place/ancient-Egypt/The-Second-Intermediate-Period
notes: Core = Itjtawy (capital at 1700 BCE). 13th Dynasty lasted to c.1650-1630 BCE (database end too early); Memphite region then under Hyksos. Ryholt: Hyksos conquest; Ben Tor: prior abandonment for Thebes. 14th Dynasty breakaway preceded.

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Qajar dynasty' - https://www.britannica.com/topic/Qajar-dynasty
source2: Mohammad Javad Sheikh-ol-Islami, 'Aḥmad Shah Qājār', Encyclopaedia Iranica - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/ahmad-shah-qajar
notes: Majles deposed Ahmad Shah and ended Qajar rule (31 Oct 1925), entrusting government to PM Reza Khan; Constituent Assembly crowned him. Constitution, Majles and ministries continued. Prior crises: Constitutional Revolution, 1909 deposition, WWI occupation, 1921 coup.

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Wang Mang' - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Wang-Mang
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Xin dynasty' - https://www.britannica.com/topic/Xin-dynasty (same publisher; no independent source could be opened)

successor: Zunghar Khanate (Galdan), then Qing after Dolon Nor 1691 and Jao Modo 1696
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Mongolia: The ascendancy of the Manchu' - https://www.britannica.com/place/Mongolia/The-ascendancy-of-the-Manchu

source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Tukulor' - https://www.britannica.com/topic/Tukulor (same publisher)
notes: Torodbe Muslim clerics of Futa itself, led by Sulayman Bal (from c.1769) then Abdul Kader Kane, overthrew the Denianke satigis and set up an elective almamate in 1776. Prior crises: Moorish raids and tribute, Denianke succession wars.
